condition_other: Autism Spectrum Disorder (BTBR mouse model of autism)
readout_other: Self-grooming test; open-field test; three-chamber sociability test; male-female social reciprocal interaction test with ultrasonic vocalization (USV) recording; H&E histology; cFOS immunofluorescence
direction_notes: TUS to the mPFC reduced self-grooming (repetitive behavior) in BTBR and B6 mice and increased cFOS-positive cell density (neuronal activation) in the targeted mPFC of BTBR mice; it also increased locomotion and selectively altered USV call-category/subtype distribution (more frequency-jump and step-down calls, fewer flat calls) in BTBR mice, but had no effect on anxiety-like behavior, direct social-interaction frequency/duration, or overall USV number/duration/frequency in either strain.
safety_notes: H&E staining of the same brains demonstrated preserved cortical cytoarchitecture with no overt histopathological abnormalities (Fig. 7c), indicating that TUS enhanced neuronal activation without detectable tissue damage.

exposures.label: TUS to the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC)

target.label: medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), comprising the infralimbic cortex, prelimbic cortex, and cingulate cortex

timing.protocol_description: The transducer was driven with a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of 1.5 kHz, a pulse length (PL) of 0.25 ms, a duty cycle of 37.5%, a burst duration (BD) of 0.45 s, and an inter-stimulus interval (ISI) of 2.1 s; TUS pulses were smoothed with 30% ramping to minimize unintended auditory brainstem response. The end of the ultrasonic beam (-6 dB cutout) was used to stimulate the mPFC at two stereotactic coordinates (0.64 mm and 1.78 mm anterior to Bregma, at depths of 2.5 mm and 3.25 mm respectively) to encompass the entire mPFC. TUS was applied for a total time of 15 minutes daily over five consecutive days.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Fifty-six B6 and BTBR mice were randomly divided into four groups: (i) B6 mice that received sham stimulation (B6 non-stimulated group, n = 11); (ii) B6 mice that received TUS stimulation (B6 stimulated group, n = 12); (iii) BTBR mice that received sham stimulation (BTBR nonstimulated group, n = 15); and (iv) BTBR mice that received TUS stimulation (BTBR stimulated group, n = 18) as shown in Fig. 1d-B.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Targeting was performed at two stereotactic coordinates: 0·64 mm and 1·78 mm anterior to Bregma, both at midline (Fig. 1c). The first coordinate was stimulated with a depth of 2·5 mm, and the second with a depth of 3·25 mm, to encompass the entire mPFC with TUS (Fig. 1c). TUS was applied to the mPFC for a total time (TT) of 15 minutes daily over five consecutive days.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: TUS was generated using the RK-50 stereotactic-guided focused ultrasound system (RK-50, FUS Instruments, Toronto, ON, Canada), a function generator (Siglent SDG 1032X, Shenzhen, China), a custom 46 dB-gain power amplifier, and 476·5 kHz single-element focused ultrasound transducer (Fig. 1a). The calibrated transducer (diameter = 35 mm, focal length = 24·5 mm, F# = 0·7) was driven at a frequency of 476·5 kHz, with a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of 1·5 kHz, a pulse length (PL) of 0·25 ms, a duty cycle of 37·5%, a burst duration (BD) of 0·45 s, and an inter-stimulus interval (ISI) of 2·1 s (Fig. 1b). The parameters were selected based on preclinical TUS studies demonstrating positive behavioral outcomes in neurological disorders.<sup>37–39</sup>

flags.reason: Paper gives TUS-treated group sizes across two separate cohorts (pilot: 3 BTBR stimulated; main cohort: 12 B6 stimulated, 18 BTBR stimulated) but never states a combined total of TUS-exposed animals; reported as a list rather than summed.

Paper states sham mice underwent identical preparatory procedures but TUS/Bregma registration was applied only to stimulated mice; it does not describe whether a transducer was present but inactive for sham mice, so mechanism is undescribed.
Paper does not state whether the reported Ispta/Isppa/pressure values at the -6dB beam cutout are free-field (water) or in-situ (brain) measurements; recorded as unspecified domain.
Effects were heterogeneous across behavioral domains (reduced grooming, increased locomotion, no anxiety effect, selective USV changes); classified as mixed_or_unclear.
